questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Sections' feature in MS PowerPoint when managing a large presentation?

options.text: To create hyperlinks between different parts of the presentation
To divide the presentation into logical groupings for better organization and navigation during editing and presenting
To apply different themes to specific groups of slides
To enable collaborative editing of specific parts of the presentation by different users

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Sections' feature in MS PowerPoint enables users to **organize large presentations** into manageable and logical groupings.
 
• It helps in **streamlining navigation** during both the editing and presentation phases by dividing the slides into distinct sections.
 
• Sections allow users to **focus on specific parts** of the presentation without being overwhelmed by the entire slide deck.
 
• This feature is particularly useful when dealing with **complex or multi-topic presentations**, ensuring better structure and clarity.
 
• Users can **rename, collapse, or expand sections** for easier navigation, enhancing productivity in managing large presentations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slide Organization in PowerPoint**

 
 
• PowerPoint includes features like 'Sections,' 'Slide Sorter View,' and 'Outline View' to help users manage and organize content efficiently.
 
• 'Slide Sorter View' provides a thumbnail view of all slides, enabling easier rearrangement.
 
• 'Outline View' focuses on text content, offering a structured view of the presentation.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Using Sections**
 
 
• Enhances collaboration when working on different parts of the presentation.
 
• Improves workflow by allowing users to concentrate on specific sections.
 
• Reduces clutter and simplifies navigation in presentations with numerous slides.
 
 
 
• **Other Navigation Features in PowerPoint**
 
 
• Slide Master: Helps maintain consistent design across slides.
 
• Hyperlinks: Facilitates linking between slides or external resources.
 
• Slide Zoom: Enables focused navigation on specific slides during presentations.
 
 
 
• **PowerPoint for Large Presentations**
 
 
• For presentations with hundreds of slides, features like 'Sections' and 'Slide Sorter View' are essential for effective management.
 
• Grouping slides into sections ensures logical flow and improved audience engagement.

questions.question: Which Indian state does the Thar Desert primarily cover?

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is the 17th largest desert in the world and primarily spans the state of **Rajasthan**, covering approximately 60% of its area.
 
• It also extends into parts of **Gujarat**, Punjab, and Haryana, but Rajasthan is the main state covered.
 
• Rajasthan's districts such as Jaisalmer, Barmer, Bikaner, and Jodhpur are most heavily impacted by the Thar Desert's arid conditions.
 
• The desert lies in the northwestern part of India and is bordered by the Aravalli mountain range in the southeast.
 
• The Thar Desert plays a crucial role in shaping the geography, climate, and cultural heritage of Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate:** The Thar Desert experiences extreme temperatures, ranging from 50°C during summers to near freezing in winters.
 
• **Vegetation:** It is characterized by xerophytic vegetation such as cacti, acacias, and thorny bushes adapted to arid conditions.
 
• **Economy:** Agriculture in the Thar region relies heavily on irrigation systems like the Indira Gandhi Canal, while tourism plays a significant role in districts like Jaisalmer.
 
• **Wildlife:** The desert is home to unique wildlife such as the Great Indian Bustard, Blackbuck, and Desert Fox, protected under various conservation initiatives.
 
• **Human Settlements:** Despite the harsh conditions, the desert supports a dense population, with many villages practicing traditional lifestyles and crafts such as pottery and textiles.

questions.question: The Cornwallis Code, introduced in 1793, is known for _______.​

options.text: establishing uniform police and judiciary reforms
introducing English as the court language

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**establishing uniform police and judiciary reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cornwallis Code, introduced in **1793**, marked a significant step in British administrative reforms in India.
 
• This code established **uniformity in police and judiciary systems**, laying the foundation for modern legal and administrative systems in India.
 
• It emphasized the separation of **revenue collection and judicial functions** to avoid conflicts of interest.
 
• District judges were made independent of the revenue administration, ensuring impartial judicial processes.
 
• The code also introduced **strict regulations for the conduct of officials**, aiming to curb corruption and inefficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Cornwallis**

 
 
• He served as the Governor-General of Bengal from **1786 to 1793**.
 
• Known as the "father of civil services in India," he introduced reforms to make administration more efficient and accountable.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Reforms under Cornwallis**
 
 
• The establishment of **civil and criminal courts** at different levels (district, provincial, and Sadar levels).
 
• District judges were appointed, and the concept of **rule of law** was strengthened.
 
 
 
• **Police Reforms**
 
 
• The police system was reorganized, and **thanas (police stations)** were established to maintain law and order.
 
• The officers were made accountable, and their powers were clearly defined.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Cornwallis Code**
 
 
• It laid the groundwork for the **Indian Penal Code** and the modern judicial system in India.
 
• The reforms also influenced subsequent British administrative practices in the country.

questions.question: Which factor primarily contributed to the development of nucleated settlements in the Bundelkhand region of central India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nucleated settlements in the Bundelkhand region primarily developed due to **security concerns and invasions**, especially during historical periods marked by frequent conflicts and raids.
 
• The settlements were designed as compact clusters to facilitate defense mechanisms and collective safety against external threats.
 
• Bundelkhand's geographical location, surrounded by rugged terrain, made it vulnerable to invasions, necessitating closely-knit communities for protection.
 
• Historical records indicate that fortifications and defensive structures were often built in conjunction with these settlements to ensure security.
 
• The prevalence of such settlements during medieval times was a strategic response to safeguard inhabitants from both human threats and environmental adversities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleated Settlements:**

 
 
• Nucleated settlements are characterized by houses grouped closely together, often around a central feature like a fort, market, or temple.
 
• These settlements are common in regions where people need to stay united for social, economic, or security reasons.
 
 
 
• **Historical Invasions in Bundelkhand:**
 
 
• Bundelkhand faced invasions from various rulers, including Mughals, Afghans, and Marathas, leading to the need for defensive settlements.
 
• Fortifications like the Kalinjar Fort were built to protect inhabitants from external threats.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Influence:**
 
 
• The rugged terrain of Bundelkhand provided natural barriers but also isolated communities, making compact settlements a necessity.
 
• Limited agricultural potential in the region further emphasized the need for cooperative living in nucleated clusters.
 
 
 
• **Defensive Architecture:**
 
 
• Structures like forts, watchtowers, and walls were integral to nucleated settlements, ensuring collective security.
 
• These architectural features are still evident in Bundelkhand's historical sites.

questions.question: The 1991 economic reforms in India led to rapid industrialisation and expansion of energy-intensive sectors. Which market-based mechanism has India adopted to balance industrial growth, energy efficiency and emissions?​

• The Perform, Achieve, and Trade (PAT) scheme is a market-based mechanism introduced by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) under the National Mission on Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE).

• Industries that achieve energy efficiency targets earn tradable Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts), which can be sold to entities that fail to meet their targets.

• The scheme helps India balance industrial growth with energy efficiency and reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, aligning with sustainable development goals.

• These certificates are awarded to industries that exceed their energy savings targets under the PAT scheme.
 
• ESCerts can be traded on power exchanges, incentivizing industries to adopt energy-efficient technologies.
 
 
 
• **National Mission on Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE):**
 
 
• NMEEE is one of the eight missions under India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).
 
• Its goal is to promote energy efficiency and reduce the energy intensity of India's economy.
 
 
 
• **Market-based Mechanism:**
 
 
• The PAT scheme is an example of a market-based approach to address environmental challenges.
 
• It incentivizes industries to achieve energy efficiency through tradable certificates rather than penalties.
 
 
 
• **Impact of PAT Scheme:**

• It has helped industries adopt advanced technologies and improve competitiveness in global markets.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios would most effectively necessitate the use of a three-dimensional reference within an MS Excel formula

options.text: Applying conditional formatting to a range of data based on values in another worksheet within the same workbook
Creating a chart that visualizes data points sourced from several different workbooks
Calculating the average sales figures across multiple non-contiguous worksheets for the same product category
Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A three-dimensional (3D) reference in MS Excel is used to reference the same cell or range of cells across multiple worksheets within the same workbook.
 
• It is particularly useful for performing calculations (e.g., summing, averaging) that involve data stored in the same cell position across identically structured worksheets.
 
• The correct scenario here—"Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year"—requires referencing the same cell (e.g., B2) across worksheets such as "Jan," "Feb," "Mar," etc.
 
• An example of a 3D reference formula for summing cell B2 across worksheets "Jan" to "Dec" would be: =SUM(Jan:Dec!B2).
 
• This method simplifies complex calculations and avoids manually navigating to each worksheet, making it efficient for managing large datasets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **3D Reference in MS Excel**

 
 
• A 3D reference allows users to refer to the same range or cell across multiple worksheets.
 
• It is denoted by the syntax: Sheet1:SheetN!CellReference.
 
• Common functions used with 3D references include SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, and MIN.
 
 
 
• **Conditional Formatting vs. 3D References**
 
 
• Conditional formatting applies visual formatting rules to data within a single worksheet or across specific ranges, but it does not use 3D references.
 
• 3D references are designed for computations rather than formatting tasks.
 
 
 
• **Identically Structured Worksheets**
 
 
• These are worksheets that share the same layout, such as having the same rows, columns, and headings.
 
• Identical structure is a prerequisite for effectively using 3D references.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of 3D References**
 
 
• Enables efficient data analysis across multiple worksheets.
 
• Reduces redundancy by avoiding repetitive formulas for each worksheet.
 
• Improves consistency and minimizes human error in calculations.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of 3D References**
 
 
• 3D references cannot be used in array formulas or with certain Excel features like Data Tables.
 
• Deleting or rearranging worksheets within the referenced range may lead to formula errors.

questions.question: India's demographic profile on the eve of independence reflected the socio-economic backwardness caused by colonial rule. Which of the following options best describes the health care and literacy statistics on the eve of independence?

options.text: High life expectancy with high birth rates and low death rates
High life expectancy with low birth and death rates
Moderate life expectancy with declining birth and death rates
Low life expectancy with high birth and death rates

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4,On the eve of independence, India was characterized by poor healthcare and literacy outcomes due to colonial exploitation. Below are key points and additional information to understand this further:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Life expectancy at birth during India’s independence (1947) was estimated to be around **32 years**, which is considered extremely low compared to global standards.
 
• Birth rates and death rates were both **high**, indicative of poor healthcare infrastructure and lack of access to medical facilities.
 
• Infant mortality rates were alarming, with nearly **150-200 infant deaths per 1,000 live births**.
 
• Literacy rates were abysmally low, with only **around 12% of the population being literate**, reflecting widespread educational deprivation.
 
• The colonial government focused primarily on revenue generation and military needs, leaving public health and education severely neglected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Life Expectancy**

 
 
• Life expectancy serves as an indicator of the general health and living conditions in a country.
 
• India’s low life expectancy at independence reflected widespread poverty, malnutrition, and limited access to healthcare.
 
 
 
• **High Birth and Death Rates**
 
 
• High birth rates were driven by social and economic factors such as lack of contraception and the need for large families in agrarian societies.
 
• High death rates were caused by rampant diseases like malaria, cholera, and tuberculosis, compounded by poor sanitation and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Infant Mortality**
 
 
• Infant mortality refers to the death of children under one year of age per 1,000 live births.
 
• India’s high infant mortality rate at independence underscored the lack of maternal and child healthcare services.
 
 
 
• **Colonial Impact on Education**
 
 
• Colonial policies largely ignored mass education, focusing instead on creating a small class of elites for administrative purposes.
 
• The absence of widespread educational initiatives led to the low literacy rates observed at independence.
 
 
 
• **Post-Independence Reforms**
 
 
• After independence, India embarked on initiatives to improve healthcare and education, such as the establishment of primary schools and public health programs.
 
• These efforts contributed to gradual improvements in life expectancy and literacy rates over the decades.

questions.question: Which policy of the British greatly affected the tribal landholding patterns and led to widespread discontent among the tribes, thereby fueling rebellions
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Forest laws and land settlements** introduced by the British led to the alienation of tribal lands and disruption of traditional tribal practices.
 
• The British declared vast areas of forests as reserved or protected, prohibiting tribal communities from practicing shifting cultivation, hunting, and gathering.
 
• Land settlements imposed by colonial authorities forced tribals into exploitative relationships with moneylenders and landlords, further marginalizing them.
 
• These laws deprived tribes of their access to resources, leading to widespread discontent, loss of livelihood, and eventual uprisings such as the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) and Munda Rebellion (1899-1900).

questions.question: The President of India possesses the power to remove or recall officials such as Governors and Ambassadors. This power is exercised based on the advice of:​

__
 
• The President of India, as the head of the state, exercises executive powers, including the removal of officials like Governors and Ambassadors, based on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
 
• This advisory role of the Union Council of Ministers is mandated by Article 74(1) of the Indian Constitution, which states that the President must act in accordance with their advice.
 
• The Union Council of Ministers is headed by the Prime Minister, who communicates decisions and advice to the President on behalf of the council.
 
• The removal or recall of Governors and Ambassadors is an executive action that reflects the collective will of the council in alignment with constitutional provisions.

• It mandates the President to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as its head.
 
• The advice tendered by the council is binding on the President.
 
• This ensures the functioning of the parliamentary system where the real executive authority lies with the council.
 
 
 
• **Role of Governors in India:**
 
 
• Governors serve as the constitutional head of a state, appointed by the President.
 
• They hold office during the pleasure of the President and can be removed based on the Union Council of Ministers' advice.

• Sound waves are mechanical waves, meaning they require a medium to travel through and cannot propagate in a vacuum.
 
• An elastic medium is necessary for the transmission of sound, as it allows the particles within the medium to oscillate and transfer energy between them.

• **Speed of Sound:** The speed of sound varies depending on the medium; it is fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases.
 
• **Vacuum:** Sound cannot propagate in a vacuum because there are no particles to oscillate and transfer the energy of the wave.

questions.question: Which of the following statements DOES NOT describe the primary difference between SRAM and DRAM in terms of their internal architecture and performance characteristics?

options.text: DRAM is much faster because it has a simple design and doesn’t need refresh.
DRAM uses one transistor + one capacitor (1T1C) per cell (high density), while SRAM uses multiple transistors per bit (lower density).
SRAM is faster and more expensive → used for CPU caches; DRAM is slower and cheaper → used for main memory (RAM).
SRAM uses more transistors per bit, yielding faster access than DRAM.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1) “DRAM is much faster and doesn’t need to refresh.”**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Why Option 1 is invalid:** *DRAM* is **slower** than SRAM and it **does require periodic refresh** to retain data. The statement reverses both facts.
 
• **Actual DRAM cell:** Typically **1 transistor + 1 capacitor (1T1C)** per bit → *high density, low cost*, but needs refresh → *higher latency* than SRAM.
 
• **Actual SRAM cell:** Typically **multiple transistors (≈6T)** forming a bistable latch → *no refresh needed, faster access*, but *lower density and higher cost*.
 
• **Common usage:** *SRAM* → CPU **caches** (L1/L2/L3). *DRAM* → system **main memory** (DIMMs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (Correct statement):** DRAM uses **1T1C** (compact, dense), while SRAM uses **multiple transistors** per bit (less dense).
 
• **Option 3 (Correct statement):** *SRAM* is faster and more expensive → used for **cache**; *DRAM* is slower and cheaper → used for **main memory**.
 
• **Option 4 (Correct statement):** SRAM’s multi-transistor latch enables **faster access** than DRAM’s capacitor-based cell.
 
• **Performance note:** Refresh operations and sense-amp charging in DRAM introduce extra delay; SRAM reads/writes directly from a stable latch.

questions.question: Which Indian Constitution Act provides for the minimization of inequalities in income, property, facilities and opportunities in the Directive Principles of State Policy?

• The amendment emphasized **social, economic, and political justice**, aligning with the goals of a **welfare state**.
 
• It also added provisions related to the protection and improvement of the **environment**, safeguarding of **forests** and **wildlife**, and promotion of **equal justice**.
 
• The **42nd Amendment** was passed during the period of **Emergency (1975–1977)** under the leadership of then **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**.
 
• Through this amendment, the words **“Socialist”** and **“Secular”** were also inserted into the **Preamble** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The amendment also added the words **“co-operative societies”** in **Article 19(1)(c)** and inserted **Article 43B** as part of DPSPs.
 
 

 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment 2002**__

 __

• It inserted **Article 21A** into the Constitution and amended **Article 45** and **Article 51A**.
 
• This was a crucial step in achieving **universal elementary education** in India.

• It also safeguarded **Article 352** by making the proclamation of **Emergency** more difficult.

• NTFS supports features like file permissions, encryption, and large file sizes.
 
• It enforces character restrictions to maintain system integrity and compatibility.
 
 
 
• **Reserved Characters:**
 
 
• Characters like **asterisks (*)** and **question marks (?)** are used as wildcards in search and command-line operations.
 
• Other reserved characters include **angle brackets ()** for redirection and **pipes (|)** for command chaining.
 
 
 
• **File Naming Best Practices:**
 
 
• Use descriptive names to make files easier to identify.
 
• Avoid excessively long file names, as some applications may face issues handling them.
 
• Stick to alphanumeric characters, underscores (_), and hyphens (-) for compatibility across different systems.

• Windows prohibits file and folder names like **CON, PRN, AUX, NUL**, and others, as they are reserved for system devices.

questions.question: How are the proceedings and status of a Lok Adalat treated under Indian law?

options.text: Proceedings are judicial and Lok Adalat is deemed a civil court under CrPC.
Proceedings are advisory and Lok Adalat is not considered a civil court.
Proceedings are not judicial and have no legal standing in courts.
Proceedings are informal and not recognised under any law.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proceedings are judicial and Lok Adalat is deemed a civil court under CrPC.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lok Adalat is a statutory body under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**, established to provide speedy and amicable resolution of disputes.
 
• The proceedings of Lok Adalat are judicial in nature, and it functions as a civil court as defined under the **Code of Civil Procedure (CrPC).**
 
• Decisions made by Lok Adalat are legally binding, and the awards are enforceable as a decree of a civil court.
 
• Cases resolved in Lok Adalat are free from appeal unless parties find the outcome unsatisfactory and choose to pursue regular court proceedings.
 
• Lok Adalat promotes alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms to reduce pendency in courts and ensure quick access to justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987:**

 
 
• It provides for the establishment of Lok Adalats and other institutions to ensure access to justice for all, particularly underprivileged sections.
 
• The Act empowers Lok Adalat to resolve disputes amicably through compromise and conciliation.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• Lok Adalat can handle cases related to civil disputes, family matters, motor accident claims, and small offenses not involving serious penalties.
 
• It cannot handle non-compoundable criminal cases.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• It is cost-effective and eliminates lengthy court procedures.
 
• Parties save time and resources while ensuring resolution through mutual understanding.
 
 
 
• **Binding Nature of Lok Adalat Awards:**
 
 
• The decision of Lok Adalat is binding on all parties and holds the same status as a civil court decree.
 
• Parties retain the option to approach regular courts if dissatisfied, but appeals are rare due to the participatory nature of the process.

questions.question: Which cytoskeletal protein is the major component of neurofilaments that helps maintain the caliber and integrity of large axons?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Neurofilament proteins** are intermediate filaments specifically expressed in neurons and are essential for maintaining the structural integrity and diameter of axons.
 
• Neurofilaments are composed of three primary subunits: **NF-L (light chain), NF-M (medium chain), and NF-H (heavy chain)**, which together form a stable cytoskeletal network.
 
• These proteins are particularly abundant in large axons and play a critical role in axonal transport and neuronal signaling.
 
• Neurofilaments contribute to the mechanical strength of axons, ensuring their resilience and ability to transmit signals efficiently across long distances.
 
• Mutations or abnormalities in neurofilament proteins are linked to neurodegenerative conditions such as **Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cytoskeletal Proteins:**

 
 
• These are structural proteins responsible for maintaining the shape, structure, and organization of cells.
 
• The major cytoskeletal proteins include **actin filaments, microtubules, and intermediate filaments**.
 
• Intermediate filaments like neurofilaments are unique to specific cell types, such as neurons.
 
 
 
• **Axonal Transport:**
 
 
• Axonal transport refers to the active movement of organelles, proteins, and other cellular materials along the axon.
 
• It is vital for neuronal function and relies on cytoskeletal structures like microtubules and neurofilaments.
 
 
 
• **Neurodegenerative Disorders:**
 
 
• Neurodegenerative diseases like ALS and Alzheimer's are associated with cytoskeletal dysfunction and aggregation of proteins.
 
• Research on neurofilaments helps in understanding the pathology of these disorders.
 
 
 
• **Intermediate Filaments:**
 
 
• Intermediate filaments provide mechanical support to cells and are more stable than actin filaments and microtubules.
 
• They are categorized into different types based on the cell type, such as keratin in epithelial cells and neurofilaments in neurons.

questions.question: What are the units for base quantities called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental or base units**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Base quantities are physical quantities that are defined independently and are used as the foundation for other derived quantities.
 
• The units for these base quantities are known as **fundamental or base units**.
 
• Examples of base units include the meter (m) for length, kilogram (kg) for mass, and second (s) for time.
 
• The **International System of Units (SI)** is the globally accepted standard that defines these fundamental units.
 
• The SI system includes seven base units, which are used worldwide for scientific and technical purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Base Quantities:**

 
 
• These are quantities like length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.
 
• They are considered independent and form the foundation of the measurement system.
 
 
 
• **SI Base Units:**
 
 
• The seven SI base units are: meter (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol), and candela (cd).
 
• Each unit corresponds to one of the seven base quantities.
 
 
 
• **Derived Units:**
 
 
• Derived units are formed by combining base units according to the relationships between physical quantities.
 
• Examples include the newton (N) for force and the joule (J) for energy.
 
 
 
• **History of SI Units:**
 
 
• The SI system was officially adopted in 1960 at the 11th General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM).
 
• It has since become the most widely used measurement system globally.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Standard Units:**
 
 
• Standardized units ensure consistency and comparability in measurements across different regions and disciplines.
 
• They are crucial for scientific research, trade, and technological development.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Dandi March of 1930?

(a)The march started from Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi, covering a distance of 240 miles.

(b) The Dandi March led to the signing of the Poona Pact
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dandi March was a non-violent protest led by Mahatma Gandhi as part of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
 
• The march began on 12th March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram near Ahmedabad and ended at Dandi, a coastal village in Gujarat, covering a distance of 241 miles.
 
• The primary objective of the march was to protest against the British salt monopoly and the imposition of tax on salt.
 
• The Dandi March is considered a pivotal event in India's struggle for independence as it mobilized mass participation.
 
• Statement (b) regarding the Poona Pact is incorrect because the Poona Pact was signed in 1932, unrelated to the Dandi March.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement:**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930 as a non-violent campaign against British rule.
 
• Focused on breaking unjust laws, such as the salt tax, and boycotting British goods and institutions.
 
• The movement significantly contributed to raising national consciousness and mass participation.
 
 
 
• **Salt Tax:**
 
 
• Imposed by the British colonial government, forcing Indians to purchase salt from British-controlled sources.
 
• Seen as exploitative and symbolized the broader economic injustices of colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Poona Pact:**
 
 
• An agreement signed in 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar regarding the reservation of seats for depressed classes in the legislature.
 
• It is unrelated to the Dandi March and occurred two years later.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Dandi March:**
 
 
• Inspired civil disobedience campaigns across India against various colonial laws.
 
• Highlighted the power of non-violent protest in challenging oppressive regimes.
